bull.b: A $176B backlog and Q2 bookings up 88% supply multiyear revenue visibility that supports durable production plans, service annuities, and margin leverage. Large contracted equipment and services reduce near-term demand exposure and allow operational scaling and disciplined capital allocation.

Rapid Electrification growth, higher margins and a larger equipment backlog indicate structural demand for grid modernization and datacenter electrification. Durable higher-margin mix supports sustained EBITDA contribution and recurring service revenue as installed base grows.

A conservative leverage profile and expanding equity provide financial flexibility for capex, R&D and buybacks while limiting refinancing risk. This balance-sheet strength underpins the company’s ability to fund scale-up of gigawatt output and absorb project-level execution variability.

bear.b: Sustained weakness and material losses in Wind depress consolidated profitability and cash conversion. Persistent project losses and reduced onshore orders mean Wind is a recurring drag that could limit company-wide margin improvement and require continued capital or restructuring to return to breakeven.

Sharp year-over-year free-cash-flow swings and weaker operating cash relative to reported earnings imply working-capital or one-time effects. This volatility raises execution and cash-conversion risk, complicating capital allocation and making sustained buybacks/dividends dependent on repeatable cash generation.

bear.t: Execution & Policy Risks in Wind/Onshore US
bear.b: Permitting, tariff uncertainty and rising offshore project costs create structural timing and cost risks for project execution. Such regulatory and project-cost headwinds can delay deliveries, inflate margins, and magnify working-capital needs across multi-year projects, pressuring durable profitability.
